referee_caveats_inferred: Molecular gas masses and radial profiles rely on CO(4-3) rather than CO(1-0) or CO(2-1), assuming a spatially uniform excitation ratio r_4,1 = 0.33 and constant Milky Way alpha_CO; radial excitation gradients (hinted at by the longer PdBI CO(2-1) scale length in the Cosmic Snake) could artificially steepen the CO(4-3) profile.
Dust mass radial profile in the Cosmic Snake assumes a radially constant dust temperature (T_dust = 38 K) and emissivity (beta = 2.2) derived from the galaxy-integrated FIR SED.

For the Cosmic Snake arc, radial profiles are measured only on the northern half of the galaxy that is lensed into the fold/cusp arc, whereas integrated properties come from the northeast counter-image.
